ledger.claim: This is one trip on all three data artifacts: trip_record, gps_trace and fare_breakdown each carry trip_id TRP-00312, and the recording windows align — trip_record.started_at is 2026-08-14T20:11:43+08:00 and gps_trace.first_fix_at is 2026-08-14T20:11:43+08:00, with the trace closing at 20:35:43, the trip's ended_at. POL-RD-08(a) is satisfied on matching identifier and matching start timestamp, so the rider's initial burden is discharged and the driver must now point to a specific artifact and a specific clause rather than assert that traffic was bad or that the destination changed.

The threshold test under POL-RD-01 must be run on gps_trace.trace_distance_km, which is 17.57 km for this trip; trip_record.actual_distance_km (17.6 km) is the rounded convenience copy of the same measurement and POL-RD-01 forbids citing it for the threshold test. Against the booked optimal of 12.5 km the trace shows an excess of 5.07 km, or 40.56% of optimal, and both POL-RD-01 gates pass: 40.56% is greater than 20%, and 5.07 km is greater than 0.8 km absolute.

The rider did move the pin mid-trip and the record shows it: the dropoff was amended at 2026-08-14T20:14:43+08:00, and trip_record.amended_optimal_distance_km is 14.0 km with amended_optimal_duration_min 19.0. Under POL-RD-05 the POL-RD-01 test is re-run between the amended endpoints, and it still passes: 17.57 km less 14.0 km leaves 3.57 km of excess, 25.5% of the amended optimal, above both the 20% and the 0.8 km gates. The destination change therefore accounts for 1.5 km of the 5.07 km measured excess and no more; the surviving 3.57 km is not explained by it, and the driver's own words say why.

The driver put the surviving excess in writing at 20:26:43: 'sorry sorry i miss the exit at braddell, go one big round come back'. That is a driver admission in the chat_log, which POL-RD-07(ii) names as an INDEPENDENT corroborating source, and it is the corroboration POL-RD-08 requires beyond the gps_trace in this case: rider_profile.deviation_claims_60d is 5 and rider_profile.deviation_claims_60d_substantiated is 0, so a surviving excess below 30% — this one is 25.5% — needs a source outside the trace. That requirement is met here, not failed: the corroboration is the driver's own admission that he missed the exit and went the long way round for that reason.

The trace is not impaired for policy purposes under POL-RD-07(a) to (c): 145 fixes at a 10 s sampling interval across 100% coverage, with gaps empty and max_gap_sec 0.0, so there is no gap above 90 seconds, no straight-line jump above 500 m and no sustained sampling interval above 30 seconds. The deviation is therefore established on the trace itself, the straight-line fallback in POL-RD-07(i) is never needed, and the rider's case does not rest on any impaired artifact.

The driver's answer in his statement — 'Route is different when destination changes' — is already spent by POL-RD-05, which absorbs only the 1.5 km the re-quoted destination adds, and it cannot be stretched further into a rider-requested detour under POL-RD-04. The rider's message at 20:14:33 names Junction 8 but carries waypoint_hint null, and no road is named, so the 200 m corroboration test in POL-RD-04 is undecidable on this record, the clause is unavailable, and POL-RD-04 excludes no distance at all from the measured excess.

Nothing on the driver's side reduces the excess. EV-ADVIS-00312-01 is MISSING — admissibility status MISSING, weight_multiplier 0.0, issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT — so no traffic advisory covers the SLE/CTE corridor in this window, and the derived advisory block returns an empty advisory list for the trip. Under POL-RD-13 the POL-RD-03 exoneration comparison cannot be run on the record and any external-cause assertion carries no weight under POL-RD-08. The absence is itself citable and is cited here; no payload is claimed from the missing artifact.

No POL-RD-10 trigger fires and the case is ruleable on the money. The trip identifiers match across all three artifacts, so POL-RD-10(2) is clear; the trace is unimpaired, so POL-RD-10(3) is clear; no party cited the missing advisory as an exculpatory artifact, so POL-RD-10(5) is not engaged, exactly as POL-RD-13(1) provides; no charge line in the fare_breakdown lacks a counterpart in the trace or the trip record (erp_gantries is empty and off_optimal_route_total is 0.00); and the computed refund is far below SGD 150.00 and below charged_total. There is no basis for ESCALATE and the rider asks the tribunal to rule.

ledger.claim: The remedy is arithmetic under POL-RD-02, run against the amended optimal route that POL-RD-05 supplies. recomputed_fare = (3.80 base fare + 0.75 x 14.0 km + 0.28 x 19.0 min = 19.62) x the 1.0 surge_multiplier recorded on the fare_breakdown — that artifact is where POL-RD-02 reads the multiplier from — plus 0.80 platform fee, 0.00 ERP and tolls, 0.00 properly chargeable fixed surcharges, 0.00 waiting_time_fee, less 0.00 promo_discount = 20.42. charged_total is 24.52 and is undisputed, so the refund is 24.52 - 20.42 = 4.10. That clears the SGD 0.50 de minimis floor and is 16.7% of charged_total, nowhere near the 90% that would make it a FULL_REFUND. The rider seeks PARTIAL_REFUND of SGD 4.10.

The rider does not claim the POL-RD-06 uplift, because the record does not support it: driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 0 against 260 completed_trips_90d, so neither limb of the pattern test is met, and in any event the surviving deviation — 3.57 km, 25.5% of the amended optimal — is neither above 50% nor above 8.0 km, so it is not a MATERIAL deviation. The remedy stays the POL-RD-02 partial rather than FULL_REFUND, and no driver-conduct referral follows on this record.

There is no counter-claim to set against the refund. The rider was billed 17.6 km of distance while the trace records 17.57 km, so the unbilled shortfall POL-RD-04 requires for DRIVER_COMPENSATION — more than 1.0 km of billed-distance shortfall — does not exist, and no payment to the driver arises on this trip.

The counterparty statement asks the tribunal to 'check her record' and brands the rider a weekly complainer. POL-GEN-01 forbids deciding on that: prior_disputes_filed (9), prior_disputes_upheld (1), rating (4.12), cancellation_rate and lifetime_trips are context only and may never ground a finding, and the driver's own prior_deviation_flags (0) is a lifetime counter that is not the deviation_flags_90d POL-RD-06 asks for. The only rider profile fields any clause may use are deviation_claims_60d and deviation_claims_60d_substantiated, for POL-RD-08 alone, and on this record they are answered — not aggravated — by the driver's own chat admission.

ledger.claim: The dropoff on this trip was amended after booking, so the POL-RD-01 threshold test must be re-run against the amended endpoints. The chat log records the rider writing at 20:14:33, 'sorry uncle change to bishan junction 8 instead of amk hub, i updated the pin' (MSG-00312-001), and the trip record stores dropoff_amended_at 20:14:43 with amended_optimal_distance_km 14.0 and amended_optimal_duration_min 19.0. POL-RD-05 requires POL-RD-01 to be re-applied against the optimal route between those amended endpoints, and POL-RD-01 requires materiality to be assessed on the excess REMAINING after a POL-RD-05 adjustment. The governing baseline is therefore 14.0 km, not the 12.5 km booked optimal, and the derived deviation block computed against 12.5 km is not the governing figure. The clause is runnable here and POL-RD-10(5) is not engaged, because amended_optimal_distance_km is non-null.

Measured against the amended baseline, the excess is the trace distance of 17.57 km less the amended optimal of 14.0 km, i.e. 3.57 km, or 25.5% of the amended optimal. That clears the establishment gate in POL-RD-01 (over 0.8 km and over 20%) but fails BOTH materiality gates — 50% of optimal and 8.0 km absolute. This is therefore a non-material deviation: no POL-RD-06 uplift to FULL_REFUND is available on this trip's evidence and no material-deviation conduct referral arises. The rider's own claim_text measures the trip the same way, saying 17.6 km was driven for a trip that 'should be 14'.

Even on the platform's own derived figures computed against the 12.5 km booked optimal, the excess is 5.07 km and 40.56% (EV-GPS-00312, derived.deviation.excess_km and excess_pct). Those figures sit below both materiality gates of POL-RD-01 — 8.0 km absolute and 50% of optimal — so on no view of the baseline is this a MATERIAL deviation, and the POL-RD-06 pattern machinery cannot be triggered into an uplift or a referral by treating it as one.

No repeat-deviation pattern is established on the driver's profile. driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 0 and driver_profile.completed_trips_90d is 260, so neither limb of POL-RD-06 is met: no 3-or-more trailing flags, and a ratio of 0.00 against a 0.05 threshold on well over the 40 completed trips the clause requires. Under POL-GEN-01 only those two fields may be used for this test; no other field on either profile may carry an adverse finding, and none is relied on here.

The refund under POL-RD-02, run against the POL-RD-05 amended route as that clause requires, is arithmetic: recomputed_fare = (3.80 + 0.75 x 14.0 + 0.28 x 19.0) x the 1.00 surge_multiplier recorded on the fare breakdown + 0.80 platform fee + zero ERP = 20.42; charged_total is 24.52; the refund is 24.52 less 20.42 = 4.10, already a multiple of SGD 0.05. That is 16.7% of charged_total, so it is a PARTIAL_REFUND and not a FULL_REFUND, and it is above the SGD 0.50 de minimis floor. It is the figure the rider's own 'should be 14' measure produces, and it does not support the SGD 6.00 contested.

No pass-through correction can be added on top of that figure. The fare breakdown carries no ERP gantry lines at all and tolls_erp of 0.00, and the trip neither originates nor ends at an airport, so no airport surcharge is chargeable. POL-RD-09(1) forbids counting off-route ERP twice on top of a POL-RD-02 refund, and there is nothing on these lines to correct. The distance-and-time refund computed above is the whole of the money in this case.

The rider's claim is subject to the additional corroboration requirement in POL-RD-08: rider_profile.deviation_claims_60d is 5 and rider_profile.deviation_claims_60d_substantiated is 0, and the excess remaining after the POL-RD-05 adjustment (25.5%) is below 30%. The only corroboration beyond the trace on this record is the driver's own chat admission of the missed Braddell exit (MSG-00312-003). The clause forbids using this factor to deny an otherwise proven claim, so it does not defeat the claim — but it does hold the rider to the measured arithmetic on the corroborated excess of 3.57 km rather than to the SGD 6.00 asserted.

The driver's chat message MSG-00312-003 ('sorry sorry i miss the exit at braddell, go one big round come back') is an admission and the driver does not dispute it. I concede that discrete error: it is a missed exit, not an unjustified route, and its distance is already comprehended within the 3.57 km excess measured against the amended optimal. That admission does not support the rider's wider contention that the whole 17.6 km was improper, and no artifact on the record measures the excess on the amended baseline any higher than 3.57 km.

The GPS trace is not impaired for policy purposes, so the case can be ruled on it directly. It carries 145 fixes at a 10 second cadence with 100% coverage, no gaps at all and max_gap_sec of 0.0. None of the POL-RD-07(a) to (c) limbs fires — no gap over 90 seconds, no straight-line jump over 500 m, no sampling interval over 30 seconds — so the independent-corroboration requirement in POL-RD-07(ii) does not arise and the POL-RD-10(3) escalation route is not available on this trace.

I disclose that EV-ADVIS-00312-01 is MISSING with weight_multiplier 0.0 and issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT: no traffic advisory covers this trip window. No party asserts a traffic cause — the driver's counterparty statement rests on the recorded mid-trip destination amendment, which is a field on the trip record — so POL-RD-03 cannot be run on this bundle and no party has invoked an exculpatory clause against a cited artifact. Under POL-RD-13 that is a gap in the bundle and not a contradiction in it, and the POL-RD-10(5) escalation trigger is not engaged.
